 Diwali bank holiday: November 9 or 10, when are banks closed for Diwali? Check RBI’s full November holiday calendar here
 Check full list of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bank holiday calendar for November 2026 below 
 Moneycontrol News 
 October 27, 2026 / 13:17 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Customers can use net banking, mobile banking apps, UPI, ATMs and other digital channels on bank holidays 
 November is packed with festivities and bank branches will observe a good share of holidays. Diwali, Guru Nanak Jayanti and schedules weekends off will amount to branches across cities staying shut for 15 days this month. 
 Bank Diwali holiday may differ for different cities: some cities will observe it on November 9, while some on November 10. Here is the full list of bank holidays in November 2026, according to the RBI calendar: 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 November 8 : Sunday 
 November 9 : Bank branches across Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Imphal, Jaipur, Kanpur, Lucknow will be closed for Diwali/Laxmi Puja (Deepawali)/Govardhan Pooja/Vishwakarma Day. 
 November 10 : Banks in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai and Nagpur will be shut for Diwali (Bali Pratipada)/Deepawali (Govardhan Puja)/Laxmi Puja/Vikram Samvant New Year Day 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 November 11 : Banks in Gangtok, Imphal, Kanpur, Kolkata, Lucknow and Shimla will be closed for Laxmi Puja (Deepawali)/Ningol Chakkouba/Bhratridwitiya/Bhaidooj/Chitragupt Jayanti

 November 13 : Banks in Shillong will remain closed for Wangala Festival 
 November 14 : Second Saturday 
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Novmeber 15 : Sunday 
 November 16 : Branches across Patna and Ranchi will observe a holiday for Chhath Puja/Surya Shashti Dala Chhath (Prath Arghya) 
 November 20 : Banks in Dehradun will be closed for Igas-Bagwal 
 November 22 : Sunday 
 November 23 : Banks in Shillong will be shut for Seng Kut Snem 
 November 24 : Branches across Aizawal, Belapur, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Hyderabad, Itanagar, Jaipur, Jammu, Kanpur, Kohima, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, New Delhi, Raipur, Ranchi, Shimla and Srinagar will observe a holiday for Guru Nanak Jayanti/Karthika Purnima/Rahas Purnima 
 November 27 : Banks in Bengaluru will be shut for Kanakadasa Jayanthi 
 November 28 : Forth Saturday 
 November 29 : Sunday 
 Even with banks closed, customers can use net banking, mobile banking apps, UPI, ATMs and other digital channels as usual. 
 Services such as fund transfers, bill payments and balance checks will remain available, unless scheduled for maintainance or mentioned otherwise. However, transactions that depend on bank clearing systems may face delays during that holidays. 
 Customers who need branch-dependant services, such as demand drafts, locker access, KYC updates or large cash transactions should plan ahead and complete them before the relevant holiday.
